nodes.name: One-step hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni foam was cleaned with HCl and ethanol, then used for one-step hydrothermal synthesis of N,F-FeO(OH)-CO3-NF. Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, urea (CH4N2O), and NH4F were used as precursors with Ni foam substrate. Through the one-step hydrothermal reaction in a high-pressure Teflon reactor for 8 h, a layer of yellow film (N,F-FeO(OH)-CO3-NF) is grown on the Ni foam. NH4F and urea act as structural guides for the two-dimensional (2D) nanosheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show cross-nanosheet array structure of N,F-FeO(OH)-CO₃-NF with thickness approximately 2 μm growing on Ni foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of Figures 1b,c show the microstructure of N₃F-FeO(OH)-CO₃-NF from the front and side. The thickness of N,F - FeO(OH) - CO₃ - NF growing on Ni foam is approximately 2μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show sheet-like cross shape with lattice fringes corresponding to FeOOH (110) and (112) crystal planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d shows the TEM image of the whole microscopic morphology. Figure 1e shows that the sample has a sheet-like cross shape.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice fringes dominated by (110) and (112) crystal planes of FeOOH PDF#46-1315 with disordered lattice waves indicating oxygen defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes are dominated by a and b crystal planes in the red box enlarged area of Figure S4a, corresponding to the crystal planes of FeOOH PDF#46-1315 (112) and (110)... disordered lattice 'waves' distributed in the ordered lattice fringes are observed in Figure S4a.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show mixed phase of FeOOH matching PDF#46-1315 and PDF#34-1266 with weak peaks and increased unit cell parameters due to N,F,CO₃²⁻ doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S7a shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of N,F - FeO(OH) - CO₃ - NF... The relatively weak peaks correspond to the FeOOH standard cards PDF#46-1315 and PDF#34-1266, showing that the sample is a mixed phase of FeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows strong broad absorption band 3500-3000 cm⁻¹ for O-H stretching, peak at 1350 cm⁻¹ for ν(CO₃), and 1650 cm⁻¹ for O-H stretching confirming carbonate presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The strong and broad absorption band of 3500 - 3000 cm⁻¹ is associated with the O-H stretching mode of the hydroxide layer. The peak around 1350 cm⁻¹ corresponds to the stretching vibration of ν (CO₃) and that around 1650 cm⁻¹ corresponds to the stretching vibration of O-H.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows C 1s peaks at 283.80, 284.57 eV (sp² C-C), 285.35 eV (C-O), 288.09 eV (C=O) confirming CO₃²⁻; F 1s at 685.15 eV; Fe 2p at 712.20/725.89 eV for Fe(III)-O; N 1s at 399.69 eV (N-metal), 407.75 eV (N-O); O 1s with O4 at 532.56 eV indicating oxygen defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2b, the C 1s peak is divided into four peaks; the peaks of 283.80 and 284.57 eV correspond to sp²C - C 285.35 eV to C - O and 288.09 eV to C = O... The peak of F 1s at 685.15 indicates that F is incorporated into FeO(OH).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX confirms uniform distribution of elements C, N, O, F, and Fe in the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elements C, N, O, F and Fe are uniformly distributed in the sample, as shown in Figure S5b-f. The energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum of N,F-FeO(OH)- CO₃-NF further proves the existence of various elements in Figure S6.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows absorption near g = 2.26 confirming presence of oxygen defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the EPR analysis, there is absorption near g = 2.26, indicating the existence of oxygen defects in N₃F - FeO(OH) - CO₃ - NF (Figure S9a).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives double-layer capacitance Cdl = 4.62 mF·cm⁻² from which ECSA is calculated, indicating highest ECSA among compared catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S18a-c show the CV curves of N,F-FeO(OH)-CO3-NF... with different scan rates. Figure S18d shows that the electric double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of N,F-FeO(OH)-CO3-NF is 4.62 mF·cm⁻²...
